example_sentences.english: I read books every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日本[にほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で面白い雑誌を読みました。
example_sentences.english: I read an interesting magazine at the library.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で面[おも]白[しろ]い雑[ざっ]誌[し]を読[よ]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がその手紙を読みましたか。
example_sentences.english: Who read that letter?
example_sentences.furigana: 誰[だれ]がその手[て]紙[がみ]を読[よ]みましたか。

items.mnemonic_text: A brush (聿) laid over a sunny page: writing.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You're at your desk when a sun, that window with a bar in it, slowly sinks below your notebook. As its last light hits the page, your hand starts to move on its own, filling line after line. That daily sun-to-paper ritual is how you learn to write.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa, the fire-breathing crow, lands on your notebook and squints at your terrible handwriting, muttering "しょ, しょ" every time you smudge a letter. Each little puff of flame dries the ink so you can keep writing.
items.description: Means "write"; shows up in words about writing, documents, and books, like 書く (to write).

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I will read a book at the library.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に手紙を書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a letter to a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: かばんに辞書を入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put the dictionary in my bag.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんに辞[じ]書[しょ]を入[い]れました。

items.mnemonic_text: An ear (耳) inside the gate (門): listening for who is there.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You press your ear right up against a gate to catch the whispers on the other side. The wood is cold, but you hold still, straining that one ear against the swinging doors. When you press an ear to a gate like this, you're doing two things at once: you hear, and you're dying to ask what's going on.
items.reading_mnemonic: Mon-Bun, the scholarly rabbit twins, press their ears to the gate to hear you ask a question — and immediately start arguing about the answer. "ぶん!" they squeak in unison, because those two never agree on anything they overhear.
items.description: Means "hear" or "ask" and shows up constantly in the verb 聞く (to hear, to listen, to ask) and in words like 新聞 (newspaper).

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝ラジオを聞きます。
example_sentences.english: I listen to the radio every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]ラジオを聞[き]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は朝、新聞を読みます。
example_sentences.english: My father reads the newspaper in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は朝[あさ]、新[しん]聞[ぶん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 鳥の声が聞こえます。
example_sentences.english: I can hear birds singing.
example_sentences.furigana: 鳥[とり]の声[こえ]が聞[き]こえます。

items.mnemonic_text: A crossroads where you choose to go.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a stick figure caught mid-stride, legs split wide, one arm swinging forward — the whole character leans into the step. That's a person who won't stand still, always moving to the next place. When you see this shape, you see someone about to go.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, can't sit still either — the second a shelf goes empty he's out the door to go restock it, muttering "こう, こう, keep it moving." Wherever he needs to go, he goes at a run.
items.description: Means "go" and shows up constantly in verbs of movement and travel, such as 行く (to go).

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、銀行に行きました。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I went to the bank.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、銀[ぎん]行[こう]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 家族と飛行機で旅行します。
example_sentences.english: I will travel by airplane with my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]と飛[ひ]行[こう]機[き]で旅[りょ]行[こう]します。

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、行ってきます。
example_sentences.english: I'm off, Mom.
example_sentences.furigana: お母[はは]さん、行[い]ってきます。

items.mnemonic_text: A tree of grain drawing people to come.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a tree standing at a crossroads with two little travelers resting under its branches, one on each side of the trunk. The tree can't move, so it waves the travelers over: "Come! Come to me, sit in my shade." Everyone always comes to the tree.
items.reading_mnemonic: The traveler who comes to the tree is Rye, and he never arrives quietly — he shouts "らい, I'm here!" as he strolls up the path. Whenever someone comes into view down the road, listen for that らい.
items.description: Means "come" and shows up constantly in the verb 来る (to come) and in time words like 来年 (next year) and 来週 (next week).

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、誰が来ますか。
example_sentences.english: Who is coming tomorrow?
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、誰[だれ]が来[らい]ますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 来月、日本へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to Japan next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]、日本[にほん]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、新しい先生が来ます。
example_sentences.english: A new teacher will come next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、新[あたら]しい先[せん]生[せい]が来[らい]ます。

items.mnemonic_text: A broom and a stop: sweeping up and returning home.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a weary traveler with a walking stick slung over one shoulder, striding toward the little house that fills the right side of this character. After a long day, the whole shape leans homeward — feet turning, roof waiting. That pull back to the front door is the feeling of return.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki, the tree spirit, has been out riding the wind all day, and now she giggles as she slips back inside her old tree with a soft き. Watch her return home and you'll hear that き every time.
items.description: Means "return," as in going or coming back home; the core kanji in the verb 帰る, to return.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は早く家に帰ります。
example_sentences.english: I will return home early tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は早[はや]く家[いえ]に帰[かえ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 遅いですから、一緒に帰りましょう。
example_sentences.english: It's late, so let's go home together.
example_sentences.furigana: 遅[おそ]いですから、一[いっ]緒[しょ]に帰[かえ]りましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、お帰りなさい。
example_sentences.english: Welcome back, dad!
example_sentences.furigana: お父[ちち]さん、お帰[かえ]りなさい。

items.mnemonic_text: Two mountains stacked, something pushing out.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look closely and you see one mountain stacked right on top of another mountain — two sets of three peaks piled up. When the peaks get that tall, there's only one thing you want to do: get out and leave. So this doubled-up mountain means exit, leave.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the exit of the mountain trail stands a hiker who sneezes so hard every time someone leaves — a huge "しゅつ!" — that the whole vending machine rattles. Every time you head for the exit, you hear that "しゅつ" behind you.
items.description: Means exit or leave; shows up in everyday words about going out, leaving, and departures.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、手紙を出します。
example_sentences.english: I will send a letter tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、手[て]紙[がみ]を出[だ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、何時に家を出ますか。
example_sentences.english: What time do you leave the house every day?
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]、何[なに]時[じ]に家[いえ]を出[で]ますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の出口はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the station exit?
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の出[で]口[ぐち]はどこですか。

items.mnemonic_text: A person ducking under a doorway to enter.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Watch the shape closely: it's a little figure ducking their head as they pass under a low doorway. You lean, you dip, you step through — and just like that, you enter.
items.reading_mnemonic: The figure ducking through the door is a new student, and as they enter the echoing school hallway everyone whispers "the new one, にゅう, the new one." Every time someone new enters, that にゅう ripples down the hall.
items.description: Means "enter" and shows up in words about entering, entrances, and admission; on'yomi にゅう, kun'yomi はい.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と一緒に店に入りました。
example_sentences.english: I entered the shop with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に店[みせ]に入[い]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーに砂糖を入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put sugar in the coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: コーヒーに砂[さ]糖[とう]を入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の入口はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the station's entrance?
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の入[いり]口[ぐち]はどこですか。

items.mnemonic_text: An eye (目) on legs going out to see.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take an eye (目) and stand it up on a pair of human legs (儿), and suddenly it can walk around anywhere it wants. Where does an eye on legs go? Out into the world, to look at everything. So this is what it means to see.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ken, the sword-collecting dog, drags you over to his wall of antique swords because he wants you to see his newest one. "けん! けん!" he barks, pawing at the blade until you finally look.
items.description: Means "see" and is the base of the common verb 見る (to see/look); it shows up constantly in everyday words about looking and watching.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日テレビを見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch TV every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]テレビを見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: ここから山が見えます。
example_sentences.english: You can see the mountain from here.
example_sentences.furigana: ここから山[やま]が見[み]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に新しい写真を見せました。
example_sentences.english: I showed the new picture to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に新[あたら]しい写[しゃ]真[しん]を見[み]せました。

items.mnemonic_text: A foot planted firmly: stop.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You're mid-stride down the mountain trail when you plant one foot flat and hard against the ground and freeze in place. That single planted foot is the whole picture: it's rooted, going nowhere. A planted foot means stop.
items.reading_mnemonic: Right where you stopped, you hear a sharp "し!" — someone shushing you. It's the vending machine at the top of the trail, hissing "し, し" as it refuses to dispense until you stop and wait. That shushing し is the sound to hold onto.
items.description: Means "stop" and is the base of common verbs like 止まる and 止める, showing up anywhere something halts or is brought to a halt.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前にバスが止まりました。
example_sentences.english: The bus stopped in front of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]にバスが止[と]まりました。

example_sentences.japanese: ここでタクシーを止めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop the taxi here.
example_sentences.furigana: ここでタクシーを止[と]めてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い時計が止まりました。
example_sentences.english: The old clock stopped.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い時計[とけい]が止[と]まりました。

items.mnemonic_text: A person standing on the ground line: to stand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a person planted firmly on the ground, feet apart, refusing to budge — they stand there, solid and upright. That single image, a person rooted on the earth, is the whole character: to stand.
items.reading_mnemonic: A soldier named Ritsu snaps to attention on the mountain trail, standing so straight you could measure a wall against him. Every time someone shouts "りつ!" he stands up even taller.
items.description: Means "stand"; a common N5 kanji appearing in words about standing up, standing something upright, and establishing or setting things in place.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はドアの前に立っています。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is standing in front of the door.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]はドアの前[まえ]に立[た]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は立って、窓を開けました。
example_sentences.english: I stood up and opened the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は立[た]って、窓[まど]を開[あ]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: あそこに男の人が立っています。
example_sentences.english: A man is standing over there.
example_sentences.furigana: あそこに男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が立[た]っています。

items.mnemonic_text: Two people (人) sitting on the earth (土) under a roof.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture two people who came inside from the cold, both dropping down onto the same patch of earth to warm up. They plant themselves right on that soil, side by side, and refuse to get up. When two bodies settle onto the earth like that, all they want to do is sit.
items.reading_mnemonic: The person who settles onto that patch of earth is Zara, and the moment she sits she lets out a long, satisfied "ざあ" of relief. Every time you see someone plop down here, you hear Zara's ざ.
items.description: Means "sit"; shows up in words about sitting down, seats, and taking a seat.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がここに座りましたか。
example_sentences.english: Who sat here?
example_sentences.furigana: 誰[だれ]がここに座[すわ]りましたか。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫が机の下に座っています。
example_sentences.english: The cat is sitting under the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]が机[つくえ]の下[した]に座[すわ]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の隣に座りました。
example_sentences.english: I sat next to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の隣[となり]に座[すわ]りました。

items.mnemonic_text: A person (人) leaning on a tree (木): resting.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You're on the mountain trail and you spot a person (left) who has slumped sideways against a tree, leaning into the trunk with its roots and branches like it's the comfiest chair in the world. A person plus a tree they're propped against — that's someone taking a well-earned rest.
items.reading_mnemonic: The hiker leaning on that tree lets out a huge, happy sigh — "きゅう!" — the sound of every muscle finally letting go. Every time you picture that person melting into rest, you hear that きゅう escape.
items.description: Means "rest" and shows up in everyday words for taking breaks and days off, like 休み.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、仕事を休みます。
example_sentences.english: I will take a day off from work tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、仕[し]事[ごと]を休[やす]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: ここでちょっと休みましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's rest here for a bit.
example_sentences.furigana: ここでちょっと休[やす]みましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪で学校を休みました。
example_sentences.english: I took a day off from school because of a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]で学[がっ]校[こう]を休[やす]みました。

items.mnemonic_text: A mouth releasing lines of speech: to say.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the bottom of this character and you'll find a mouth, wide open. Above it, stacked up in neat horizontal lines, is everything that mouth is pushing out — layer after layer of speech. A mouth releasing stacked lines like that is exactly what it means to say a word.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, a general in full armor climbs the mossy steps and won't stop giving orders — every word out of his mouth is a barked command. The cats scatter as the general says "げん!" like it's the only word he knows.
items.description: Means "say" or "word"; the base of many speech-related kanji and words like 言語 (language) and the verb 言う (to say).

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は何と言いましたか。
example_sentences.english: What did the teacher say?
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は何[なに]と言[い]いましたか。

example_sentences.japanese: この言葉の意味が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand the meaning of this word.
example_sentences.furigana: この言[こと]葉[ば]の意[い]味[み]が分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は面白いことを言います。
example_sentences.english: He says interesting things.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は面[おも]白[しろ]いことを言[い]います。

items.mnemonic_text: A net (罒) over money (貝): buying with cash.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You spot something you want, so you reach for the cowrie shell that once worked as money. You lay that shell on the counter and slide it across. Handing over the shell-money is how you buy.
items.reading_mnemonic: The moment you buy your onigiri at Koichi's konbini, Kaa the fire-breathing crow swoops in and shrieks 「ばい」 as if saying "bye-bye" to your cash before you've even paid.
items.description: Means "buy," the verb 買う (to purchase); shows up constantly in shopping and everyday transactions.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、新しい本を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new book yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、新[あたら]しい本[ほん]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日に友達と買い物に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went shopping with a friend on Sunday.
example_sentences.furigana: 日[にち]曜[よう]日[ひ]に友[とも]達[だち]と買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、母とデパートで買い物します。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, I will shop at the department store with my mom.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、母[はは]とデパートで買[か]い物[もの]します。

items.mnemonic_text: Goods laid out on a stand: selling.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a street vendor with a wide table: a little lid or sign propped up top, a body of stacked goods below, and two legs kicked out to the sides as he leans back. He's got everything laid out and he's shouting prices at the crowd. That's the whole posture of someone whose only job is to sell.
items.reading_mnemonic: The vendor keeps yelling one thing at every customer who walks past: "Buy! ばい, ばい, one for you and one for the baby!" He'll sell to anyone who slows down, and every pitch ends on that same ばい.
items.description: Means "sell"; shows up in売る (to sell) and in compounds about buying and selling like 売店 (shop, stand).

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に自転車を売りました。
example_sentences.english: I sold my bicycle to a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に自[じ]転[てん]車[くるま]を売[う]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで服を売っています。
example_sentences.english: They sell clothes at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートで服[ふく]を売[う]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: その車は売りません。
example_sentences.english: I will not sell that car.
example_sentences.furigana: その車[くるま]は売[う]りません。

items.mnemonic_text: A roof over a heap of good rice: food to eat.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the whole character as a little tent pitched over a full table: the peaked roof on top, and underneath it a heaped tray of rice and side dishes. It's the family shelter you duck into when you're hungry — a roof made entirely of dinner. Under that roof there's only one thing to do: eat the food.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cheerful line cook at Koichi's konbini slings hot lunches under the fluorescent lights, and every time a tray lands he shouts his catchphrase: しょく, しょく, come and get it! You hear しょく and your stomach knows it's time to eat.
items.description: Means eat or food; shows up in everyday words for meals, eating, and food, and as the verb "to eat."

example_sentences.japanese: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of food do you like?
example_sentences.furigana: どんな食[た]べ物[もの]が好[す]きですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 家族と一緒にレストランで食事します。
example_sentences.english: I will dine at a restaurant with my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]にレストランで食[しょく]事[じ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、パンを食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat bread every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]、パンを食[た]べます。

items.mnemonic_text: Food (食) beside a person yawning (欠) for a drink.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the left is the radical for food and eating, and on the right is a person opening their mouth wide in a yawn, a lack. But this yawning mouth isn't tired — it's tipping a glass back, mouth wide open to gulp something down. When you see food beside that gaping, thirsty mouth, you drink.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini a regular named Inn slaps a cold can on the beeping till and says the same thing every single day: "First, I drink!" You can hear the 「いん」 right at the front of Inn's name as he cracks it open.
items.description: Means "drink"; the everyday kanji in the verb 飲む, to drink.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink coffee every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]コーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たい飲み物が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a cold drink.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たい飲[の]み物[もの]が欲[ほ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、友達とお酒を飲みました。
example_sentences.english: I drank alcohol with my friend yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、友[とも]達[だち]とお酒[さけ]を飲[の]みました。

items.mnemonic_text: A ray of sunlight so bright it turns white.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You step outside Koichi's konbini and the morning sun hits you full in the face — a ray of light so bright everything goes pure white for a second. You blink, and the whole world is still washed out and white. That blinding ray is your picture for white.
items.reading_mnemonic: The dazzling light spooks a startled hawk perched on the konbini roof; it beats its wings once and goes, はく, hacking out a cough as it flaps into the too-bright sky. Hear that はく every time you see this pure white flash.
items.description: Means white; a very common kanji seen in words for the color white and in names.

example_sentences.japanese: その白い靴は新しいですか。
example_sentences.english: Are those white shoes new?
example_sentences.furigana: その白[しろ]い靴[くつ]は新[あたら]しいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の映画は面白かったです。
example_sentences.english: The movie yesterday was interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]の映[えい]画[が]は面白[おもしろ]かったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の車は白です。
example_sentences.english: My car is white.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の車[くるま]は白[しろ]です。

items.mnemonic_text: The earth glowing under a big fire: red.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the ground cracking open on the mountain trail, and underneath it the Earth is glowing — lit from below by a fire you can't see. That heat pushes up through the soil until the whole hillside burns a deep, angry red. Earth glowing under a fire: red.
items.reading_mnemonic: The guy who lit that underground fire is Seki, and he's coughing his lungs out from the smoke — a wet, rattling せき that won't stop as long as the red embers keep burning. Every time he sees red he starts up again: せき, せき, せき.
items.description: Means "red"; a common color kanji that shows up in words for the color itself and things like traffic lights.

example_sentences.japanese: あの赤ちゃんはかわいいです。
example_sentences.english: That baby is cute.
example_sentences.furigana: あの赤[あか]ちゃんはかわいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は赤い車が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a red car.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は赤[あか]い車[くるま]が欲[ほ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: そのかばんは赤です。
example_sentences.english: That bag is red.
example_sentences.furigana: そのかばんは赤[あか]です。

items.mnemonic_text: A fresh sprout over the moon: the blue-green of youth.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a tiny sprout pushing up over the moon. It's young, fresh, and glowing that impossible color between blue and green — the shade of new leaves at dusk. That youthful sprout-over-moon is blue-green.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei, the star student, holds up a jar of blue-green ink and says the color is called 「せい」 — of course she knew it first. She's already dipping her perfect brush in before anyone else can answer.
items.description: Means blue or green (the fresh blue-green range); shows up in color words and in compounds about youth and freshness.

example_sentences.japanese: あの青いペンを借りました。
example_sentences.english: I borrowed that blue pen.
example_sentences.furigana: あの青[あお]いペンを借[か]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい青い車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new blue car.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい青[あお]い車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 青と白の服を着ます。
example_sentences.english: I will wear blue and white clothes.
example_sentences.furigana: 青[あお]と白[しろ]の服[ふく]を着[ちゃく]ます。

items.mnemonic_text: A sooty village over a fire: black with smoke.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the whole village at dusk, its wooden houses caked in soot, huddled over one big cooking fire. The smoke has stained every wall until the sooty village over a fire is one single color: black.
items.reading_mnemonic: The soot-covered villagers cough up thick black lungfuls, hacking こく, こく into the night air. Every cough is darker than the last — that's the sound of black.
items.description: Means "black"; the everyday word for the color (くろ) and a common on'yomi こく in compounds.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の車は黒です。
example_sentences.english: My car is black.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の車[くるま]は黒[くろ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あの黒い犬はかわいいです。
example_sentences.english: That black dog is cute.
example_sentences.furigana: あの黒[くろ]い犬[いぬ]はかわいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は黒板に書きました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher wrote on the blackboard.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は黒[こく]板[ばん]に書[か]きました。

items.mnemonic_text: A tall tower with windows: high and expensive.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the tall tower with windows standing over the town — but notice the open mouth at its base, an entrance yawning wide for anyone brave enough to climb. It's the fanciest, most expensive building around, and everyone cranes their neck to see how tall it is.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, is jealous of that tall tower, so he stacks his onigiri shelves higher and higher until they're the tallest — and priciest — display in town. As the tower of rice balls wobbles, he shouts こう to warn a customer before it topples.
items.description: Means tall or expensive; a very common kanji appearing in words about height, price, and school (as in 高校, high school).

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、高い時計を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought an expensive watch yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、高[たか]い時計[とけい]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの山は高いです。
example_sentences.english: That mountain over there is tall.
example_sentences.furigana: あの山[やま]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランの肉は高いです。
example_sentences.english: The meat at that restaurant is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: あのレストランの肉[にく]は高[たか]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) safe under a roof: peaceful and cheap.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a woman kneeling gracefully inside a snug little house, the roof pulled down over her like a blanket. Nothing can reach her in here — she is safe, the rent is nothing, everything is calm. A woman tucked safely under a roof is cheap and peaceful.
items.reading_mnemonic: She's spreading sweet red あん (bean paste) on a bun, humming, utterly at peace. Every bite is cheap comfort — say あん and taste that calm.
items.description: 安 means cheap or peaceful, and shows up in words for low prices, safety, and being at ease.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This book is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランは安くておいしいです。
example_sentences.english: That restaurant is cheap and delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: あのレストランは安[やす]くておいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、安い靴を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought cheap shoes yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、安[やす]い靴[くつ]を買[か]いました。

items.mnemonic_text: A standing tree cut by an axe (斤): freshly new.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You walk into a showroom and there, front and center, someone is proudly standing (立) beside the thing they just built. The person planted on the ground won't stop grinning because everything here is fresh off the line — untouched, gleaming, new.
items.reading_mnemonic: The showroom greeter is Shin, and every time a new model rolls in he shouts his own name — しん! — as he yanks the cover off. Whatever Shin unveils is always brand new.
items.description: Means "new"; a very common kanji appearing in words for new things, newspapers, and freshness.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new car.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は毎朝新聞を読みます。
example_sentences.english: My father reads the newspaper every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]新[しん]聞[ぶん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: あの新しいレストランはおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: That new restaurant is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: あの新[あたら]しいレストランはおいしいです。

items.mnemonic_text: Ten (十) mouths (口) of stories passed down: old.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Above the mouth balances a little cross of stacked crossbars, like the beams of a house that's been standing for centuries. Every mouth that has passed through here has told the same worn-out story, over and over. A mouth held up by ancient timber can only mean one thing: old.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi finds an ancient rice ball at the very back of his konbini shelf, so far past its date the wrapper has yellowed. He picks it up, sighs, and mutters just one syllable at how old it is: 「こ」.
items.description: Means "old," as in old and worn from age; appears in words about age and antiquity and in the common word for "used/secondhand."

example_sentences.japanese: 古い車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought an old car.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この町には古い家がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of old houses in this town.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]には古[ふる]い家[いえ]がたくさんあります。

example_sentences.japanese: その時計は少し古いです。
example_sentences.english: That watch is a little old.
example_sentences.furigana: その時計[とけい]は少[すこ]し古[ふる]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: Two evenings (夕) stacked: many days piling up.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture two little dumplings stacked one on top of the other, leaning slightly like a lopsided snowman. One dumpling is never enough — you always want another, and then another, until the plate is piled high. Two stacked and always craving more: that's how you get many.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, Ta counts the coins in the improbable vending machine, and there are far too many to hold. "た, た, た," she taps each one as they spill from her hands — there are just too many.
items.description: Means "many" or "much"; a common N5 kanji seen in words about large quantities, such as expressing that there is a lot of something.

example_sentences.japanese: 多田さん、ここは人がたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: Ms. Tada, there are a lot of people here.
example_sentences.furigana: 多田[ただ]さん、ここは人[ひと]がたくさんいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 本多さんの町は雨がたくさん降ります。
example_sentences.english: It rains a lot in Mr. Honda's town.
example_sentences.furigana: 本多[ほんだ]さんの町[まち]は雨[あめ]がたくさん降[お]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 宇多田さんは今日仕事がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: Ms. Utada has a lot of work today.
example_sentences.furigana: 宇多田[うただ]さんは今日[きょう]仕[し]事[ごと]がたくさんあります。

items.mnemonic_text: Small (小) with a slash taken off: even fewer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take something small — that hook with two flanking dots — and slice one more dot away with a downward stroke. Now there's even less than small: barely anything left. When you take a bite out of small, what remains is few.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sho, the tiny stage magician, opens his white-gloved hand to reveal only a few crumbs of confetti — "しょう time!" he squeaks, and even the doves look unimpressed by how little there is. His whole act, like everything about him, is small and few.
items.description: Means "few" or "little"; a common N5 kanji that shows up in words about small amounts and quantities.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は少し寒いです。
example_sentences.english: It's a little cold today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は少[すこ]し寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: この本は少し高いです。
example_sentences.english: This book is a little expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は少[すこ]し高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を少し話します。
example_sentences.english: I speak a little Japanese.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]を少[すこ]し話[はな]します。

items.mnemonic_text: Flowing long hair on an elder: long and the eldest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the whole character: it's an old man standing side-on, with a flowing beard and long hair streaming down past his shoulders, and a walking stick planted at the bottom. He's the eldest, the one everyone else follows — so this is your picture of something long, and of the elder who leads.
items.reading_mnemonic: That long-bearded elder is the leader of a whole troupe of butterflies, and he lets one land on his flowing hair — a ちょう (butterfly). Every time you see this kanji, picture the ちょう resting on the leader's long locks.
items.description: Means long or leader; shows up in words for length, seniority, and being the head of something, like a school principal or a company chief.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の髪は長いです。
example_sentences.english: Her hair is long.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]の髪[かみ]は長[なが]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は長い手紙を書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a long letter.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は長[なが]い手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の話は長いです。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's stories are long.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の話[はなし]は長[なが]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) already up over the ground (十): early.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the sun — that window with a bar in it, a whole day — rising up over a stick planted in the ground. It's cresting the horizon way sooner than you expected, before your alarm even goes off. When the sun comes up that early, you're forced to move fast.
items.reading_mnemonic: There's a rooster at Grandma Kane's shrine who crows the moment the sun peeks over the mossy steps, way too early: "そう! そう!" he screams, so loud the cats scatter. Now you're up before dawn whether you like it or not.
items.description: Means "early" or "fast," and shows up in everyday words about time and speed like 早い (early/fast) and 早く (quickly).

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は早く起きました。
example_sentences.english: I woke up early today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は早[はや]く起[お]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は早いから、寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I have an early start tomorrow, so I'm going to sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は早[はや]いから、寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日早く学校へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to school early every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]早[はや]く学[がっ]校[こう]へ行[い]きます。

items.mnemonic_text: A jewel (玉) enclosed by borders: a country.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture an enclosure — a closed box with walls around everything inside. Draw those walls big enough and you're no longer fencing a garden; you're fencing a whole nation. Walls that wrap around an entire people give you a country.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the border of this walled country stands a guard named Koku, who stamps every passport with a cheerful こく sound. No stamp, no entry — こく, こく, all day long.
items.description: Means "country" or "nation"; a very common kanji seen in words for countries and citizenship, read こく in compounds and くに on its own.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、外国に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to a foreign country next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、外[がい]国[こく]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この町には外国人がたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of foreigners in this town.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]には外[がい]国[こく]人[ひと]がたくさんいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の車は高いです。
example_sentences.english: Foreign cars are expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の車[くるま]は高[たか]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: Drops falling inside a window frame from the sky: rain.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look through the window frame and watch the drops falling inside it, one after another down the glass. Those little drops caught in the frame are all you need to picture. Drops falling inside a window frame: rain.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cow gets caught outside in the downpour and lets out a long, miserable "うー" as the drops soak her. Every time it rains, that cow's soggy うー is the sound you hear.
items.description: Means "rain"; the base kanji for weather words and it sits on top of many other weather-related characters as a component.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日はたくさん雨が降りました。
example_sentences.english: It rained a lot yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]はたくさん雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は雨が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: I dislike rain.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は雨[あめ]が嫌[きら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は雨ですか。
example_sentences.english: Will it rain tomorrow?
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]ですか。

items.mnemonic_text: Rain (雨) with lightning stretching down: electricity.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A storm is hammering the rain against your window frame, drops streaking down the glass, when a jagged bolt splits the sky and lights the whole room. That flash coming out of the rain crackles with pure energy — electricity.
items.reading_mnemonic: The lightning hits a power line and the whole street goes DEN — でん — every fluorescent tube in Koichi's konbini surging bright at once. You feel that でん in your teeth as the electricity floods back.
items.description: Means "electricity"; shows up in everyday words for trains, phones, lights, and anything electrical.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝電車で会社に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I take the train to work every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]電[でん]車[しゃ]で会[かい]社[しゃ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜に母に電話します。
example_sentences.english: I'll call my mom at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]に母[はは]に電[でん]話[わ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 暗いから電気をつけます。
example_sentences.english: It's dark, so I'll turn on the light.
example_sentences.furigana: 暗[くら]いから電[でん]気[き]をつけます。

items.mnemonic_text: A cart seen from above with an axle: a vehicle.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look straight down at a cart from above: one long axle running through the middle, wheels flanking each side, a boxy frame around it all. That's exactly what this character is — a cart seen from overhead with its axle drawn right through it. Trace that shape and you're looking at a vehicle.
items.reading_mnemonic: A show-off racer revs his engine outside Koichi's konbini and shouts "Watch me!" — but he peels out so fast all you hear is a screech of "しゃ!" as the vehicle vanishes down the street. Every time you see this car kanji, that "しゃ!" is the last sound it makes.
items.description: Means car or vehicle; a common N5 kanji that appears in words for cars, trains, and bicycles.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝電車で会社に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning I take the train to the office.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]電[でん]車[しゃ]で会[かい]社[しゃ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: あの車はとても大きいです。
example_sentences.english: That car over there is really big.
example_sentences.furigana: あの車[くるま]はとても大[おお]きいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は自転車が好きです。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother likes bikes.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は自[じ]転[てん]車[くるま]が好[す]きです。

items.mnemonic_text: A horse (馬) waiting where trains stop: a station.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You're waiting on a platform when a galloping horse, flowing mane and all four legs pounding, thunders straight past you and onto the tracks. The conductor sighs — this happens every day here, horses treating the place like a pasture. Where else would a runaway horse end up but the station?
items.reading_mnemonic: A commuter named Eki misses the last train and shouts "えき! えき!" across the empty platform, hoping the station master will hear her and hold the doors.
items.description: Means "station" — the word for a train or subway station, seen constantly in place names and on transit signs.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅は家から近いです。
example_sentences.english: The station is close to my house.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]は家[いえ]から近[ちか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員に切符を見せます。
example_sentences.english: I show my ticket to the station staff.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]に切[きっ]符[ぷ]を見[み]せます。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝この駅で電車に乗ります。
example_sentences.english: I board the train at this station every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]この駅[えき]で電[でん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]ります。

items.mnemonic_text: A neck (首) moving down a path: the road and the way.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You step onto a winding road that advances up the mountain trail, twisting past every switchback. There's nothing else here but that one long ribbon of path unrolling ahead of you. Follow it and it takes you exactly where a road should — this kanji is road, or the way forward.
items.reading_mnemonic: Halfway up the road you meet a doe standing in the middle of the path, blocking the way. She won't budge, so you call out "どう do I get past you?" — and the doe just chews and stares, owning the whole road.
items.description: Means road or way; a very common kanji seen in words for streets, paths, and figurative "ways" of doing things.

example_sentences.japanese: この道は長いです。
example_sentences.english: This road is long.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は長[なが]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日道を歩きます。
example_sentences.english: I walk along the road every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]道[みち]を歩[ある]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 道の近くに公園があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a park near the road.
example_sentences.furigana: 道[みち]の近[ちか]くに公[こう]園[えん]があります。

items.mnemonic_text: A rice field (田) marked out into a town.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture this whole character as a bird's-eye view of a settlement: a neat grid of rice fields on the left pressed up against a straight main road running down the right. Fields plus a road is the smallest complete place people can live in — that's a town.
items.reading_mnemonic: The town mayor climbs onto a soapbox in the square and announces he's the big chief now: "I'm in charge — call me ちょう!" Every time you walk into this town, you hear that same booming ちょう echoing off the buildings.
items.description: Means "town" and shows up in place names and words for local districts and neighborhoods.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は賑やかです。
example_sentences.english: This town is lively.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]は賑[にぎ]やかです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、町へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to town.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、町[まち]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はこの町に住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: He lives in this town.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はこの町[まち]に住[す]んでいます。

items.mnemonic_text: A cloth over a stand where the city market gathers.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You stroll into the town square and above every stall hangs a bright piece of cloth on a rod, snapping in the wind. Each cloth marks a different seller, and rows of them stretch as far as you can see. So many stalls under so much cloth — this is the heart of the city, its bustling market.
items.reading_mnemonic: The busiest stall belongs to Shi, a sharp-eyed vendor who greets every shopper crossing the market with a cheerful 「し!」. Follow her voice and you'll always find the center of the city.
items.description: Means city or market; shows up in words for towns and municipal places like 市 (city) and city names.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこの市に住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I live in this city.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はこの市[し]に住[す]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: この市はとても大きいです。
example_sentences.english: This city is very big.
example_sentences.furigana: この市[し]はとても大[おお]きいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は市で野菜を買います。
example_sentences.english: My mother buys vegetables at the market.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は市[し]で野[や]菜[さい]を買[か]います。
